title: Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contracts — Amount of Customer-Elected Cash
content:
**§1 Authorization the cash replaces.** On a Homeowner Service Contract, the customer-elected cash is worked out from the replacement authorization most recently issued on the contract, which is the authorization the cash replaces.

**§2 Starting figure.** Its cash starting figure is the amount recorded on that replacement authorization.

**§3 Remaining benefits, counted as if reversed.** The remaining item benefit and the remaining aggregate benefit are counted as if that replacement authorization had already been reversed: the tier's cap for the covered item less the payments on that item counted toward the remaining benefits with the authorization's amount taken back out, floored at zero, and the tier's aggregate term limit less every payment on the contract counted toward them with the authorization's amount taken back out, floored at zero. The cap and the limit are the tier's figures on the Homeowner Service Contracts schedule of benefits.

**§4 Payments counted.** A payment counts toward the remaining benefits when its event date falls within the twelve months before today, that is after the same calendar day twelve months earlier, whatever term its request fell in; repair, replacement, cash-in-lieu and out-of-network payments count toward the item, supplemental allowances count toward the aggregate only, and a reversal takes its authorization's amount back out of both counts.

**§5 Result.** The customer-elected cash is the lowest of the cash starting figure, the remaining item benefit and the remaining aggregate benefit, never below zero, rounded to the cent once at the end.

**§6 Scope.** For a customer-elected settlement, and only for such a settlement, the cash paid is the customer-elected cash worked out under this section rather than an offer amount, still limited to the remaining item benefit and the remaining aggregate benefit counted as if the replaced authorization had already been reversed and still rounded to the cent; every company-elected settlement remains under the general cash-in-lieu rule. For a customer-elected settlement, and only for such a settlement, the payment is the customer-elected cash worked out under this section, with no offer to accept, and it carries the settlement basis "customer elected"; every company-elected settlement remains under the general cash-in-lieu payment rule. For a customer-elected settlement, and only for such a settlement, the item cap and the aggregate term limit are measured against the payments dated within the twelve months before today; every other payment remains measured by the term rule of the benefit caps. For a customer-elected settlement, and only for such a settlement, the item cap is still shared by every repair, replacement, cash-in-lieu settlement and out-of-network reimbursement for that item, counted over the payments dated within the twelve months before today rather than over the term; every other payment remains measured by the term rule of the benefit caps. For a customer-elected settlement, and only for such a settlement, every payment on the contract, supplemental allowances included, still counts toward the aggregate term limit, counted over the payments dated within the twelve months before today rather than over the term; every other payment remains measured by the term rule of the benefit caps. For a customer-elected settlement, and only for such a settlement, the remaining item benefit is still the item cap less the payments counted toward that item and the remaining aggregate benefit is still the aggregate term limit less the payments counted toward it, each floored at zero, with both counted over the payments dated within the twelve months before today; every other payment remains measured by the term rule of the benefit caps.

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

A Bridgewell HomeCare Gold contract (garage door opener cap 750.00, aggregate term limit 20000.00). The replacement authorization most recently issued on the contract is for the garage door opener, recorded at 620.00. In the twelve months before today the contract shows that 620.00 authorization and a 200.00 garage door opener repair, and 9,400.00 of payments in all, both of those included.

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Cash starting figure | 620.00 |
| Item payments counted, with the 620.00 taken back out | 820.00 less 620.00 is 200.00 |
| Remaining item benefit | 750.00 less 200.00 is 550.00 |
| Aggregate payments counted, with the 620.00 taken back out | 9,400.00 less 620.00 is 8,780.00 |
| Remaining aggregate benefit | 20,000.00 less 8,780.00 is 11,220.00 |
| Customer-elected cash | the lowest of 620.00, 550.00 and 11,220.00: 550.00 |

Taking the replaced authorization's own amount back out keeps the cash from being reduced by the very authorization it replaces.
